chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr [and] ibn Ali ibn Abdullah al-Basri narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Ali al-Karkhi narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq al-San'ani narrated to us, he said: Mu'ammar narrated from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) performed the dawn prayer, and when he turned from his prayer, he faced us with his noble face, in reverence to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and then he said: O people, whoever misses the sun, let him hold fast to the moon, and whoever misses the moon, let him hold fast to Venus (al-Zuhra), and whoever misses Venus, let him hold fast to the Two Farqads (the two bright stars). Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: I am the Sun, Ali is the Moon, Fatima is Venus, and Hasan and Husayn are the Two Farqads. And the Book of Allah will not be separated from them until they come to me at the Basin.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt), referring to the Prophet's family.
key_terms.الزُّهْرَةُ: Venus (the morning star), used here as a metaphor for Fatima al-Zahra.
key_terms.الْحَوْضَ: The Basin (Hawd), a reservoir in Paradise from which the Prophet will give drinks to his followers on the Day of Judgment.
key_terms.الْفَرْقَدَيْنِ: The Two Farqads (two bright stars, often identified as Aldebaran and Capella or similar), used here as a metaphor for Hasan and Husayn.

ai.seo_question: What celestial metaphors did the Prophet use to describe himself and the Ahl al-Bayt in this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith employs a celestial metaphor to establish the Ahl al-Bayt as the indispensable guides of the Muslim community, paralleling their role with the Quran's eternal presence. The identification of the Prophet as the Sun and Ali as the Moon signifies their complementary authority, while the 'Two Farqads' (Polaris) represent Hasan and Husayn as the guiding stars of the Imams. This narration underscores the theological principle that the Ahl al-Bayt and the Quran are inseparable until they meet at the Hawd, affirming their joint role in preserving divine guidance.
